# **After Hours (6775) README**

## 					      *Milestone 1*

# **Team Name**

After Hours

# **Product Name**

After Hours (mobile app)

# **Motivation**

A typical club-goer planning a night out in Singapore has no single source of information. Venue information is scattered across Telegram channels, Instagram stories, and individual club websites, each updated inconsistently and at different times.  The result is an inefficient way to gather information and compare venues. What should take seconds takes thirty minutes.

After Hours solves this by centralising Singapore's nightlife information in a single mobile application. Users can browse all active venues and events on a single calendar, compare DJ lineups, crowd levels, and other relevant information, buy and sell tickets through an in-app marketplace, and document and track their nights out with friends through a social feed.

# **Target Audience**

Young adults aged 18 to 26, primarily university students and early-career professionals, based in Singapore, who go out to clubs occasionally, roughly once a month. They are familiar enough with the local nightlife scene to know the main venues and recognise well-known DJs, but not deeply embedded enough to have insider knowledge or industry connections. They feel that planning a night out is more effort than it should be, with information scattered across multiple Telegram channels, Instagram pages, and word of mouth. Going out is inherently social for them as they go in groups, coordinate logistics over WhatsApp/Telegram, and discuss the night afterwards. 

# **User Stories** 

1.  As a university student planning a night out with friends, I want a single screen showing all venue information so that I can compare options quickly without checking multiple sources.  
2.  As a club-goer, I want to see the crowd level of a venue before going out so that I can avoid wasted trips and choose a venue that matches the energy I am looking for.  
3. As a club-goer who bought a ticket in advance, I want to list my ticket on a marketplace where buyers are already planning their night out so that I can find a genuine buyer faster than on Carousell or Telegram.  
4. As a club-goer, I want to log my nights out with photos, videos, captions, and stats so that I can look back on my experiences the way I would a personal journal.  
5. As a club-goer, I want to see lighthearted stats like my total nights out, hours spent at clubs, and blackout count so that I can laugh at my own nightlife history and share it with friends.  
6. As someone in a group chat trying to decide where to go, I want to see which venues my friends are attending so that we can coordinate without lengthy back-and-forth over WhatsApp.  
7. As a club-goer arriving at a venue, I want to know the guestlist closing time in advance so that I can plan my arrival and avoid paying door price unnecessarily.  
8. As a buyer on the marketplace, I want to see the seller's profile, activity history, and reviews before purchasing so that I can assess their credibility before committing to a transaction.  
9. As a club-goer who relies entirely on Telegram and word of mouth for nightlife information, I want a single reliable source that aggregates event details across multiple venues so that I no longer have to monitor multiple channels to stay informed.  
10. As a club-goer frustrated by long queues, I want to see real-time crowd level updates for a venue so that I can decide whether to join the queue or go somewhere else before making the trip.

# **App Features**

There are 3 main features with sub features. There are a total of 8 features of sufficient complexity.

1. **Nightlife Calendar**

<div align="center">
  <img width="499" height="830" alt="Screenshot 2026-05-31 at 5 48 50 PM" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0646356-efb4-4035-8c9d-31bab85e324b" />
</div>

   	*Figure 1.1: Venues with relevant information for decision-making*

   Unlike fragmented sources such as Telegram channels and Instagram pages, where event information is scattered and inconsistent, After Hours consolidates Singapore's nightlife events into a single calendar view. Users can browse upcoming events across multiple venues, and see real-time information including DJ lineups, crowd levels, ticket prices, and closing times,  all in one place, updated live.

   **1.2 Filtering system**

   Filter by date, crowd level, price, guestlist status and music genres. This feature is currently scoped for Milestone 2 and has not yet been implemented fully.

<div align="center">
  <img width="332" height="553" alt="Screenshot 2026-05-31 at 6 16 54 PM" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48e2941d-3f81-41d4-a3b4-4b9111778402" />
</div>

   			*Figure 1.2: Filtering venues by date allows for efficiency*

   **1.3 Full view of venue**

   Tapping on an event card navigates the user to a dedicated detail screen for that event. The screen displays the full event name, venue name and address, doors open and closing time and a short DJ biography is included to help users decide based on the performer. Two prominent action buttons are provided: one linking directly to the official ticketing page and one linking to the venue's guestlist sign-up form, displayed alongside the guestlist closing time. A sold out badge replaces the ticketing button if the event is at capacity.  This feature is currently scoped for Milestone 2 and has not yet been implemented.

   **1.4 Friends attendance**

   On the calendar screen, friends’ attendance is displayed on each event card in the form of their profile picture. Users can see which friends have marked themselves as attending the event. This feature adds a social coordination layer to the app, reducing the back-and-forth of planning a night out over WhatsApp by surfacing attendance information directly within the event context. This feature is currently scoped for Milestone 3 and has not yet been implemented.

   

   

2. **Ticket Marketplace**  
   Unlike general platforms such as Carousell or Telegram channels, After Hours provides a targeted marketplace where both buyers and sellers are verified club-goers actively planning a night out. Listings are contextualised alongside live event information, and seller credibility is established through platform activity history. This feature is currently scoped for Milestone 2 and has not yet been implemented.

   

3. **Social & Nightlife Stats**   
   **3.1 Social Feed — Post Photos and Captions**

   Tapping on the Social tab navigates the user to a feed of posts from their night out. Users can upload photos and write captions tied to a specific venue and event. Posts are visible to friends on the platform and displayed in reverse chronological order. Each post displays the venue name, event name, and timestamp alongside the photo and caption, giving context to the memory beyond a generic social media post.  This feature is currently scoped for Milestone 3 and has not yet been implemented.

   **3.2 Nightlife Stats — Track Your Nights Out**

   The profile screen shows a personalised summary of the user's nightlife activity. Tracked metrics include total nights out this month, total hours spent at clubs, and most visited venues. Lighthearted stats such as blackout and puke counts add a humorous dimension to the experience, encouraging users to engage with the feature socially. All metrics are self-reported and update automatically as the user logs attendance at events through the app.  This feature is currently scoped for Milestone 2 and has not yet been implemented.

   **3.3 Friends System**

   The friends system allows users to connect with other After Hours users on the platform. Users can send, accept, and decline friend requests through the profile screen. Once connected, friends' activity becomes visible across the app — including attendance on event cards, posts on the social feed, and nightlife stats comparisons. This feature underpins the social layer of After Hours, and is a dependency for Feature 1.4  and the friends-scoped visibility in Feature 3.1. This feature is currently scoped for Milestone 3 and has not yet been implemented.

   

# **Tech Stack**

**1\. Frontend: Flutter** Cross-platform mobile framework developed by Google. After Hours is built with Flutter to support both iOS and Android from a single codebase, using Dart as the programming language. Key packages used: `cloud_firestore` for database integration, `firebase_auth` for authentication, `intl` for date formatting, and `url_launcher` for external guestlist and ticketing links.

**2\. Backend: Firebase** Backend-as-a-service platform developed by Google that provides all server-side infrastructure for After Hours. Currently utilises two Firebase services:

* **Cloud Firestore** — NoSQL real-time database storing all app data across three planned collections: `events` (nightlife event data including venue, DJ, crowd level, time, price, and guestlist information), `users` (profile and nightlife stats), and `listings` (ticket marketplace). Data is fetched via live Firestore streams, meaning the UI updates automatically when data changes.  
* **Firebase Authentication** — Handles user login and registration via email and password, including auth state persistence across sessions.  
* **Firebase Storage (Planned — Milestone 2\)** for social feed photo and video uploads.

  **3\. Version Control: GitHub** Source code hosted on GitHub with feature-based branching. All new features are developed on dedicated branches and merged into main via pull requests with peer code review.

  **4\. Data Pipeline: Python with BeautifulSoup (Planned — Milestone 2\)** Event data is manually seeded into Firestore at Milestone 1\. From Milestone 2, a Python script using the BeautifulSoup library will scrape event listings directly from Singapore venue websites, parse the relevant fields, and write structured data to the Firestore `events` collection. The script will be run manually on a weekly basis at Milestone 2, with full scheduling automation planned for Milestone 3\.
